Disney+ and Hulu Raise Prices Again, Ad-Free Plans Now $21.49 - MacRumors

# Disney+ and Hulu Raise Prices Again, Ad-Free Plans Now $21.49

Wednesday September 23, 2026 12:10 pm PDT by Juli Clover

Disney today increased the prices on several of its Disney+ and Hulu streaming plans, with the increase coming exactly one year after Disney's last price hike.

 Premium ad-free plans are $2 to $2.50 more expensive per month, while Disney's ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu plans are $0.50 higher per month. The ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu bundle has not changed in price, and that's what Disney is steering customers toward.

- Disney+ (Ads) - $12.49, up from $11.99
- Disney+ (No Ads) - $21.49, up from $18.99
- Hulu (Ads) - $12.49, up from $11.99
- Hulu (No Ads) - $21.49, up from $18.99
- Disney+, Hulu Bundle (Ads) - $12.99, no change
- Disney+, Hulu Bundle (No Ads) - $21.99, up from $19.99
- Disney+, ESPN, Hulu Bundle (Ads) - $21.99, up from $19.99
- Disney+ (No Ads), Hulu (No Ads), ESPN Select (Ads) - $32.99, up from $29.99
- Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max Basic (Ads) - $21.99, up from $19.99
- Disney+, Hulu, HBO Max Basic (No Ads) - $34.99, up from $32.99

Bundles with ESPN or HBO Max are also $2 to $3 more expensive. Buying a standalone Disney+ or Hulu plan is just $0.50 cheaper per month than getting a bundle, both with ads and without. Disney is pushing bundles because it has been merging Hulu content into the Disney+ app to create an all-in-one experience.

When Disney+ launched in November 2019, it was priced at $6.99 per month. It did not have ads at the time, with Disney introducing its first ad-supported plan in 2022. Pricing for the no-ad option has increased more than 200% in nearly seven years.

Apple's streaming TV service launched right around the same time as Disney+ for $4.99 per month. Today, the Apple TV service is $14.99 per month, also a 200% increase. Other streaming services like Netflix and HBO Max raise prices regularly too.

Disney's higher prices go into effect for new subscribers today, and for existing subscribers on their next monthly bill.

Published Oct 11, 2026 Checked against official sources · last verified Oct 11, 2026 · how we verify

Hulu sells one streaming library at eleven different prices, depending on what you bundle with it. # Disney+ and Hulu subscriptions are about to get more expensive

Amber Neely

 Wed Sep 23 2026, 11:55 AM EDT · 1 minute read 

Disney+ and Hulu subscription prices are increasing in 2026

Disney+ and Hulu subscribers are about to pay more for their streaming services as Disney rolls out another round of price hikes. 

The increases affect both ad-supported and ad-free subscriptions, although customers who subscribe to the ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu bundle will see no change. The largest increases are coming to the standalone ad-free plans, which will each cost an additional $2.50 per month, a roughly 13% increase. 

Subscribers could begin receiving notifications about the price increases as early as Wednesday. The new prices are as follows: 

- Disney+ without ads: $21.49, up $2.50
- Hulu without ads: $21.49, Up $2.50
- Disney+ and Hulu without ads: $21.99, up $2
- Disney+ with ads: $12.49, up $0.50
- Hulu with ads: $12.49, up $0.50
- Disney+ and Hulu with ads: $12.99, unchanged

The ad-supported Disney+ and Hulu bundle is the only plan exempt from this next batch of price increases. At $12.99 per month, it costs just 50 cents more than subscribing to either service individually with ads. 

AppleInsider has some deals for new Disney+ bundle subscribers. Deals include Disney+ and Hulu for $11.99 for the first six months, or a Disney+, Hulu, and HBO Max plan starting at $19.99 per month.

# Hulu Price Per Month 2026: Every Plan and Bundle

Amit Yadav· October 6, 2026· 11 min read

15. Does Hulu have a free trial?
16. Can I download shows on Hulu with ads?
17. Why does Hulu's no-ads plan still show ads?

Hulu costs $12.49 a month with ads and $21.49 a month without ads in the US after Disney's latest price rise. New subscribers pay that now; existing members move on their first bill on or after October 21, 2026. Hulu + Live TV is $99.99 a month with ads.

Here is the twist that most price guides miss: the Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads costs $12.99, just 50 cents more than Hulu on its own, and the ad-free bundle is $21.99, also 50 cents more than ad-free Hulu. For almost everyone, buying Hulu by itself no longer makes sense. This guide covers every plan, what you actually get, the bundles, student and carrier deals, price history and who should pay for what.

Prices checked October 2, 2026

Prices from Disney's September 23, 2026 US price announcement: Hulu with ads $12.49 (was $11.99), Hulu Premium (no ads) $21.49 (was $18.99), Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads $12.99 (unchanged), bundle Premium $21.99 (was $19.99), Hulu + Live TV $99.99 with ads or $109.99 without (both up $10). Hulu's US plan page was geo-blocked from our test location, so we confirmed these against multiple reports of Disney's announcement.

The short answer

- Hulu with ads: $12.49 a month. The bundle with Disney+ is $12.99. Buy the bundle.
- Hulu Premium (no ads): $21.49. The ad-free Disney+ and Hulu bundle is $21.99. Again, buy the bundle.
- Students: the Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads is $6.49; the older $1.99 Hulu-only student plan may not be open to new signups.
- Hulu + Live TV: $99.99 with ads, and it already includes Disney+ and ESPN.
- Hulu has raised prices every October since 2021. Plan on another rise in late 2027.

## Hulu plans and what you get

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Monthly price | $12.49 | $21.49 | $99.99 with ads, $109.99 ad-free on-demand |
| Yearly cost | $149.88 | $257.88 | $1,199.88 |
| Ads | Yes | Almost none (see below) | On live channels |
| Screens at once | 2 | 2 | 2 (unlimited with add-on) |
| Downloads | No | Yes | On-demand library only |
| 4K | Select titles | Select titles | Select titles |
| Live channels | No | No | 95+ channels, cloud DVR |
| Includes Disney+ and ESPN | No | No | Yes |

### The fine print

- "No ads" is not quite no ads. A handful of shows on Hulu Premium still play short ads before and after episodes because of licensing deals. Hulu lists them with a "no ads" exception. It is a few titles, not a lot, but it surprises people.
- No downloads on the ad plan. Offline viewing is Premium-only.
- Two screens. Families with three or four TVs need the Unlimited Screens add-on, which is only available with Hulu + Live TV.
- The Hulu app is moving into Disney+. During 2026 Disney is folding Hulu content into the Disney+ app. Standalone Hulu plans are still sold, but more and more of the experience lives in Disney+, which is another reason the bundle makes sense.
- Price rises apply to existing members after a 30-day notice. There is no grandfathering.

# Disney+ and Hulu Raises Prices Again, the Fourth Hike in Four Years 

 By Todd Spangler 

### Todd Spangler

 The streamflation trend continues: Disney is once again asking Disney+ and Hulu subscribers to pay even more for the streaming service.

 Disney+ Premium and Hulu Premium, the plans without ads, are both increasing from $18.99 to $21.49/month. The Disney+/Hulu Premium Bundle is ticking up two bucks, from $19.99 to $21.99/month.

 The price increases are effective Wednesday (Sept. 23) for new subscribers. Existing customers will see the new pricing on their next monthly bill. 

 The new pricing comes as Pixar blockbuster “Toy Story 5” debuted on Disney+ on Wednesday. Variety has reached out to Disney for additional info. 

 Disney’s streaming price hikes have become an annual ritual. The latest increases mark the fourth time in four years the Mouse House is raising rates in the U.S., after price hikes for Disney+ and Hulu in October 2024 and in October 2023.

# Hulu Price Hikes & Price History (2026)

Updated October 5, 2026 · Researched & fact-checked by Shaheer

Hulu has raised prices most years since 2023. The ad-supported on-demand plan went from $7.99 to $9.99 (October 2024) and then to $11.99 (October 21, 2025), while the ad-free plan rose from $14.99 to $17.99 (October 2023) and on to $18.99 (October 2024). Disney is also merging Hulu + Live TV with Fubo.

## At a glance

Current price

$21.49 (No Ads (on-demand))

Last increase

September 23, 2026 (+13.2%)

Total change tracked

+43.4%

Tracked increases

5

## Key takeaways

- Hulu’s ad-supported on-demand plan rose from $7.99 to $9.99 (2024) and then to $11.99 (October 2025).
- The ad-free on-demand plan climbed from $14.99 to $17.99 (2023) and on to $18.99 (2024).
- Disney now raises Hulu prices roughly every October, alongside Disney+ and ESPN.
- Hulu ad-free is $21.49/month as of September 23, 2026, and the ad plan $12.49 — identical to Disney+, which rose the same amounts on the same day.
- Ad-free Hulu has gone $14.99 → $17.99 (2023) → $18.99 (2024) → $21.49 (2026), about 43% in three years.
- The ad-free Disney+/Hulu bundle at $21.99 is 50 cents more than Hulu alone — effectively Disney+ for pocket change if you already pay for Hulu.

## Hulu price increase history

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| September 23, 2026 | No Ads (on-demand) | US | $18.99 → $21.49 | +13.2% | Source |
| September 23, 2026 | With Ads (on-demand) | US | $11.99 → $12.49 | +4.2% | Source |
| October 21, 2025 | With Ads (on-demand) | US | $9.99 → $11.99 | +20% | Source |
| October 17, 2024 | With Ads (on-demand) | US | $7.99 → $9.99 | +25% | Source |
| October 12, 2023 | No Ads (on-demand) | US | $14.99 → $17.99 | +20% | Source |

## What Hulu costs right now

- With Ads (on-demand): $12.49 (US)
- No Ads (on-demand): $21.49 (US)
- Disney+/Hulu bundle (ad-free): $21.99 (US)
- Disney+/Hulu bundle (with Ads): $12.99 (US)

## Why Hulu keeps raising prices

Hulu has settled into an almost-annual October increase since Disney took full control. The ad-supported on-demand plan went from $7.99 to $9.99 in 2024 and to $11.99 in October 2025, while the ad-free plan rose from $14.99 to $17.99 in 2023 and to $18.99 in 2024, a steady upward march across both tiers.

Disney raises Hulu in lockstep with Disney+ and ESPN, steering subscribers toward bundles and the ad-supported tiers where it earns advertising on top of the subscription. The merger of Hulu + Live TV with Fubo adds another moving part for live-TV subscribers, whose package prices are higher and change more often than on-demand.

When a service raises prices on a yearly cadence, the increases stack up faster than they feel. Recording what you pay for Hulu, and which tier, makes each October bump visible instead of a quiet line-item creep on your statement.

Since the October 2025 round Disney has stopped treating Hulu and Disney+ as separately priced products. On September 23, 2026 both ad-free plans went from $18.99 to $21.49 and both ad plans from $11.99 to $12.49 — same day, same amounts. Hulu ad-free has now risen from $14.99 in 2023 to $21.49, about 43%.

The bundle maths is the part worth acting on. The ad-free Disney+/Hulu bundle is $21.99, which is 50 cents more than Hulu ad-free on its own at $21.49. If you pay for Hulu without ads and do not have Disney+, you are 50 cents away from both. The ad-supported bundle stayed at $12.99 while the two ad plans separately now cost $24.98.

### Did Hulu raise its price in 2025?

Yes. On October 21, 2025 Hulu raised its ad-supported on-demand plan from $9.99 to $11.99/month, part of a wider Disney streaming increase.

### How much does Hulu cost now?

As of 2026, Hulu’s ad-supported on-demand plan is $11.99/month and the ad-free plan is $18.99/month in the US. Hulu + Live TV costs significantly more.

results.text:
Disney+ and Hulu raise prices by up to 13 percent after doubling profits - Ars Technica

# Disney+ and Hulu raise prices by up to 13 percent after doubling profits 

 The Disney+ ad-free plan is now more expensive than Netflix’s. 

 Scharon Harding – Sep 23, 2026 5:18 pm | 126 

 

 A promotional image for the third season of The Mandalorian. Credit: Disney 

 A promotional image for the third season of The Mandalorian. Credit: Disney 

Disney+ got its fourth price hike in four years today. Hulu prices also went up.

Disney+ and Hulu’s respective standalone, ad-free plans (which also support 4K and HDR) are each increasing 13 percent from $19 per month to $21.50/month.

Disney+ and Hulu’s respective standalone plans with ads increased from $12 to $12.50.

The Walt Disney Company also increased prices for bundles of the streaming services, including those with ESPN.

The price for the Disney+ and Hulu bundle without ads increased from $20/month to $22/month. The Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads ($13) didn’t get more expensive.

However, prices increased for the Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN Select bundles with ads (from $20 to $22) and without ads (from $29 to $33).

Monthly subscription prices for Hulu + Live, which adds cable channels delivered over the Internet to Hulu’s on-demand options, went up by $10.

For comparison, Netflix is currently $9/month with ads and starts at $20/month without ads. There’s also a $27/month ad-free plan for premium features, like 4K. That means Disney+ and Hulu are both more expensive than the most popular streaming service now, unless you want 4K or HDR.

The last time that Disney+ raised prices was in October 2025. It also raised prices in October 2024, October 2023, and December 2022. It launched in 2019.

Hulu’s most recent price hikes occurred in October 2025, October 2024, October 2023, and October 2022. It launched in 2008.

Today’s price hikes follow Disney increasing the price for both tiers of its ESPN streaming service on September 17.

In its most recent quarterly earnings report, Disney reported that revenue from Disney+ and Hulu increased 11 percent. Operating income for Disney+ and Hulu combined increased 116 percent year over year to $712 million. Netflix, for comparison, reported operating income of $4.19 billion in its most recent earnings report. Netflix has many more subscribers (325 million as of January) than Disney+ (131.6 million as of September 2025) and Hulu (59.7 million subscribers for its on-demand streaming service as of September 2025).

Price hikes are likely part of Disney’s ongoing effort at streaming profitability. Netflix’s success shows there is still ample room for growth. The new prices may also steer customers more toward bundles, which streaming service providers believe lead to fewer cancellations and help Disney manage the unpredictable ads market.

Jamie Slack

September 23, 2026

Well, this is annoying. Disney+ and Hulu have new U.S. subscription prices, and the standalone no-ads plans are now $21.49 a month each. But there is one useful little wrinkle: the Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads is still $12.99 a month.

These are the prices shown on Disney’s live plan page and Hulu’s plan page on September 23, 2026. If you are already subscribed, your actual next charge depends on your plan, billing date, promotion, and whether you pay through a third party. Check the price in your account or notice before changing anything.

## What do Disney+ and Hulu cost now?

| U.S. plan | Current monthly price |
| --- | --- |
| Disney+ with ads | $12.49 |
| Disney+ Premium without ads | $21.49 |
| Hulu with ads | $12.49 |
| Hulu Premium without ads | $21.49 |
| Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads | $12.99 |
| Disney+ and Hulu bundle without ads | $21.99 |

In other words, if you already pay for one standalone service at the regular monthly price, the corresponding two-service bundle is 50 cents more per month. That is the part I would check before paying for two separate subscriptions. The ad-supported bundle remains $12.99; the no-ads bundle is now $21.99. See Disney’s current bundle terms for the exact plan descriptions.

## Did every plan go up?

No. The Disney+ and Hulu bundle with ads stayed at $12.99. The individual Disney+ and Hulu ad plans are $12.49 each, while both standalone no-ads plans are $21.49. The no-ads two-service bundle is $21.99. Disney lists its annual Disney+ Premium plan at $214.99, which is a separate option from monthly billing.

There are also limited six-month introductory prices displayed on Disney’s page: $11.99 per month for the bundle with ads and $19.99 per month for the no-ads bundle. Those offers have specific terms and then renew at the regular monthly prices of $12.99 and $21.99, respectively. Do not confuse the promotional figure with the permanent price.

## What should you check before your next bill?

- Which plan you actually have. Standalone Hulu, standalone Disney+, the two-service bundle, and Live TV are different subscriptions.
- Who bills you. App store and other partner billing can vary from direct signup pricing.
- Your next billing date and any notice. That is the best way to see exactly when a change applies to your account.
- Whether you pay for both separately. Compare your real bill to the current bundle terms before switching, especially if you have an older promotion or add-ons.

And if you came here because Toy Story 5 is finally on the service, here is our quick guide to where it is streaming. At least movie night can be the fun part of this conversation.

# Streaming prices in 2026: Netflix, Disney+, HBO Max and more

 By Yash 10 October 2026 

Published 10th October, 2026

 This article is primarily about Netflix 

- Ad-free plans for the biggest streaming services now cost $14.99 to $26.99 a month in the US
- Netflix Standard is $19.99, Disney+ and Hulu are $21.49 each, HBO Max Standard is $18.49 and Apple TV is $14.99
- Here is every major service's US price, the cheapest ad-supported options and how to cut your bill

The short answer: in the US, ad-free plans for the biggest streaming services now cost between $14.99 and $26.99 a month. Netflix Standard is $19.99, Disney+ and Hulu Premium are $21.49 each, HBO Max Standard is $18.49 and Apple TV is $14.99. Ad-supported plans start at $8.99 for Netflix and Paramount+.

The table lists advertised US monthly prices before tax. Disney's existing-subscriber changes apply on or after October 21; your billing platform and renewal date determine when they reach your account. Verify the actual checkout price before subscribing, especially when switching a carrier- or platform-billed plan.

Photo via Wikimedia Commons // An HBO Max advertisement in Krakow. HBO Max's ad-free Standard plan costs $18.49 in the US.

### What changed in 2026

Almost every service raised prices this year. Netflix increased all three plans in March, by $1 for its ad plan and $2 for both ad-free plans. Disney raised Disney+ and Hulu again in September, the fourth increase in four years, as we reported in Disney's 2026 price increase. YouTube Premium rose to $15.99, Peacock increased its plans in August and Amazon renamed its ad-free add-on Prime Video Ultra and raised it to $4.99.

Apple TV now costs $14.99 a month. Apple One, which bundles Apple TV with Apple Music and more, also rose, as our report on the Apple TV and Apple One price increase explains.

### Music streaming prices

Spotify Premium Individual costs $12.99 a month after a 2026 increase, with Duo at $18.99, Family at $21.99 and Student at $6.99. Apple Music costs $11.99 for individuals, $19.99 for families and $6.99 for students. Our comparison of Spotify and Apple Music looks beyond price.

Photo via Wikimedia Commons // The Disney+ logo. Ad-free Disney+ now costs more than three times its $6.99 launch price in 2019.

### How much is everything?

Subscribing to Netflix Standard, the ad-free Disney+ and Hulu bundle, HBO Max Standard and Apple TV costs about $75 a month before tax. Add Spotify or Apple Music and YouTube Premium and it passes $100. That is why many households now rotate services rather than keeping them all.

### Six ways to pay less

Use bundles: the Disney+ and Hulu bundle costs only 50 cents more than one service. Try ad tiers if you mainly watch in the background. Rotate subscriptions around the shows you want. Check what your phone carrier, broadband plan or credit card includes. Pay annually where a service offers a discount. And review your subscriptions every few months. On iPhone, Settings, then your name, then Subscriptions shows those billed through Apple.
